properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-11, Anthony's word: "yes, I like option A - let's implement." OPTION A CHOSEN — speak on read, gated on the hash. B, C and D are recorded below as considered and not taken.

HIS FRAMING, and it was the right diagnosis: "It sounds like we have the tool, just not used well or surfaced."

⚠️ THE TOOL WAS ALREADY BUILT. `import_graph` takes a `path`, so an agent catches a graph up with the committed record in ONE TOOL CALL and no terminal at all. The CLI flag `--import` is a second route for people without an agent, not the only one. So nothing new was needed on the doing side — only on the noticing side.

⭐⭐ THE MEASURED FINDING THAT SHAPED THE BUILD: `provenance::last_synced` — the content hash this seat believes is at a given path — was WRITTEN BY TWO PATHS AND READ BY ONE. `record_sync` is called by `export_graph` (exchange.rs:207) and by `import_graph` (exchange.rs:382); `last_synced()` was read at exchange.rs:171, inside `export_graph`, and nowhere else. **The design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last** — when you tried to export, hours later, and the stale-seat refusal finally fired. Same family as `dec:one-retire-edge`'s "a marker nothing reads is a comment", except here something did read it, at the wrong moment.

🛑 AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT THIS NODE FIRST CARRIED WAS FALSE, which is why the option was buildable at all. It said "I have unexported work" and "someone else's work has arrived" look similar from inside. They do not: `crates/reflow2-core/src/sync.rs` already distinguishes them exactly. File hash == `last_synced` ⇒ the file has not moved ⇒ every difference is the caller's OWN unexported work ⇒ silent. File hash != `last_synced` ⇒ somebody else has been there ⇒ actionable. One comparison, and no false-positive mode on solo work.

WHAT WAS BUILT: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/sync_debt.rs`, served as the `sync_status` tool and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say. One finding per file this seat has synced with — `in_step` / `behind` (the actionable one) / `moved_but_current` / `missing` / `unreadable`. The judgement is BORROWED from `sync::assess_overwrite` rather than reimplemented; this module supplies the enumeration, the gate and the wording.

WHY IT LIVES AT THE MCP LAYER: `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly (`reconcile_artifacts` makes the caller supply hashes; `granularity` and `consumption` both say so). So the check could NOT go into `loop_status` in core, and belongs in the crate that already does this comparison for `export_graph`.

📌 A COST DECISION, PINNED BY A TEST: the export needed to compare against is the expensive half and the hash check is the cheap half, so `mine` is passed as a CLOSURE and is never built on the in-step path — the one every ordinary session takes. `the_expensive_export_is_not_built_on_the_ordinary_path` makes that a guarantee rather than a style choice.

📌 THE DESCRIPTION BUDGET FORCED THE SHAPE OF THE SURFACE: `loop_status`'s tool description was already at 1493 of 1500 characters, so the contract could not be documented there. Hence a dedicated `sync_status` tool carrying the full contract, with `loop_status` carrying only the finding — which is a self-explaining English sentence and needs no schema to interpret.

WHAT WAS NOT CHOSEN, kept because the roads not taken are part of the design's memory:
- B — AUTO-IMPORT. Closest to what was first asked for. Rejected: `import_graph` is an UPSERT, so an unasked one silently overwrites live session work, and doing it unasked makes it invisible. `dec:ask-not-repair`.
- C — REFUSE ON FIRST READ. Rejected: a refusal on READ is heavy-handed, and a session deliberately working from an older design would meet it every time.
- D — DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Rejected: the answer this project has already found wanting twice; a discipline written down and not triggered is one that does not happen.

⭐ THE DEPENDENCY STILL HOLDS: if `dec:central-host` goes the hosted way for the flo2 case, this question DISSOLVES for those users — there is no local store to catch up, because there is one graph everyone reads live. It stays live for anyone working from a checkout.
properties.name: DECIDED — a graph reports when the shared record has moved ahead of it, gated on a computed content hash, and never acts on it
properties.rationale: Anthony chose option A on 2026-08-11 after being shown that the tool already existed and only the trigger was missing. `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25) had already committed this project to building "merge-on-pull ergonomics" and that clause had never been cashed, so this settles an unbuilt commitment rather than adding new scope. The node keeps its own refuted counter-argument on the record: the claim that unexported work and somebody else's arrival look alike from inside was disproved by reading sync.rs the same day, and it was that refutation which made option A buildable.
